grants.Program Focus:
OPENING SUMMARY — WEEK OF SEPTEMBER 21 – 25, 2026

Aviation Infrastructure:

FAA Contract Tower (FCT) Competitive Grant Program (DOT-FAA-26-0117-002), up to $100,000,000 in IIJA Airport Infrastructure Grant funds for airport-owned air traffic control towers, $25,000–$55,000,000. Eligibility is a closed list of 186 FCT and candidate-list airports.

Due October 19, 2026.

Clean Transportation / Air Quality:

EPA Diesel Emissions Reduction Act (DERA) National Program (EPA-OAR-OTAQ-26-01), approximately $180,000,000 — three fiscal years of funding pooled into one round, 4–12 awards per EPA Region. Region 9 carries the largest allocation ($42.6M) and the highest per-application cap ($12M). No for-profit applicants; mandatory cost share runs as high as 75% on most replacements. Due January 22, 2027.

Geothermal / Prize Competitions:

DOE Office of Geothermal GEMS Prize — a $300,000 data-science competition to map hidden geologic faults from geophysical data, individual prizes $10,000–$100,000 (LOW). Open to U.S. individuals, teams, and U.S.-based private entities. Submissions close December 3, 2026.

National Lab Commercialization:

DOE Technology Commercialization Fund CLIMR Technology Specific Lab Call (DE-LC-000L130), an estimated $33,000,000–$41,000,000. DOE labs, plants, and sites apply; companies participate as partners through the Teaming Partner List. Deadlines to be confirmed on Exchange. Concept Papers due 11/3/26; Full applications due 3/1/27.

Natural Resources:

USDA NRCS Easement Restoration and Stewardship (USDA-NHQ-ACEP-26-NOFO0001456) — $5,000,000 across one to four cooperative agreements, $250,000–$5,000,000, for four- to five-year restoration, stewardship, and monitoring work on NRCS wetland and floodplain easements. Open to for-profits, including engineering and restoration firms; no cost share. Due November 19, 2026.

California State Opportunities:

CEC GFO-26-502 Integrated Point-Source Carbon Capture and Advanced Combustion at Industrial Facilities — demonstration projects pairing capture equipment with combustion retrofits at California industrial sites. $5,992,293 in total funding; $1,000,000-$5,992,293 per award. Due January 19, 2027; questions due November 20; pre-application workshop November 4.

CalRecycle Increased Recycling of Empty Glass Beverage Containers, FY 2026–27 — $14,198,550, $250,000–$4,000,000, for bin-based glass collection from bars and restaurants. Certified recycling centers, collection programs, community service programs, and cities/counties only; 100% match required. Due October 29, 2026.

CDFA 2026 California Nutrition Incentive Program — $13,500,000, $50,000–$12,500,000, for CalFresh incentives on California-grown produce. SNAP-authorized farmers’ markets, CSAs, farm stands, and small businesses, or nonprofits applying on their behalf. Due November 3, 2026.

CNRA Youth Community Access Grant Program, Round 4 — approximately $15,000,000 in Proposition 64 funds, $30,000–$300,000, no match, for youth access to natural and cultural resources. Public agencies, nonprofits, and California Native American tribes. Due November 4, 2026.

New York State Opportunities:

NYSERDA Buildings of Excellence, Round 7 — demonstration awards up to $1,500,000 and Early Design Support awards up to $150,000 for zero-emission, resilient multifamily buildings. Due January 20, 2027.

NYSERDA Sun and Soil Program (PON 6206) — $10,000,000 multi-year agrivoltaics program covering planning, implementation, and applied research on New York farms. Round 1 due December 10, 2026; Round 2 due April 20, 2027.

grants.Description: Federal Aviation Administration — FY 2027 IIJA FAA Contract Tower (FCT) Competitive Grant Program
grants.Opportunity #: DOT-FAA-26-0117-002; Assistance Listing 20.117 (Airport Infrastructure Grants). Grants.gov opportunity 363941.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Transportation — Federal Aviation Administration, Office of Airports. Direct inquiries to the applicable FAA Regional Office or Airports District Office (or the State Block Grant Program agency), or to the FAA IIJA Team at 9-ARP-IIJAAirports@faa.gov.
grants.Total Funding: Up to $100,000,000 in FY 2027 Airport Infrastructure Grant funds, part of the up to $600 million the IIJA allocates to the FCT program over ten years. The listing does not state an expected number of awards.
grants.Award Range: $25,000 minimum to $55,000,000 maximum per the Grants.gov listing. The ceiling is more than half the round, so a single tower replacement could absorb a large share of available funds.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Airport sponsors approved in the FAA Contract Tower Program or Contract Tower Cost Share Program (49 U.S.C. § 47124) and normally eligible for AIP competitive grants (49 U.S.C. § 47115). This includes public agencies, private entities, state agencies, and Indian Tribes or Pueblos that own a public-use NPIAS airport, plus the territorial and Compact-state sponsors named in the listing.

As of January 2026, FAA counts 186 eligible airports — 163 enrolled in the FCT program and 23 on the candidate list. Eligibility is effectively a closed list; confirm a client airport appears on FAA's eligible-tower list before any outreach.
grants.Deadline:
October 19, 2026. The FAA application period opened September 18, 2026.

Applications are submitted electronically on FAA Form 5100-144 (Airport Terminal and Tower Project Information), which must be completed in Adobe rather than a web browser. Selected applicants then follow standard AIP application procedures — SF-424 and FAA Form 5100-100 — before award.
grants.Program Focus:
Airport-owned airport traffic control tower (ATCT) projects that address aging airport infrastructure. Eligible work: sustaining, constructing, repairing, improving, rehabilitating, modernizing, replacing, or relocating non-approach control towers; acquiring and installing air traffic control, communications, and related equipment for those towers; or constructing an FAA-certified remote tower with its equipment.

FAA has run this competition every year since FY 2022, and prior selection lists are posted — most recently the FY 2026 selections released May 15, 2026. Those lists are the best available guide to what scores.
grants.Cost Share / Match: The Grants.gov listing shows no cost-sharing requirement. Because selected projects convert into AIP grants before award, confirm the applicable federal share in the FY 2027 NOFO before building a budget.
grants.Primary Sector: Aviation Infrastructure; Air Traffic Control Towers; Remote / Digital Towers; IIJA Airport Infrastructure Grants; Public-Use Airports
grants.Link to NOFO: FCT on Simpler.Grants.gov; FY 2027 FCT NOFO (PDF); FAA FCT program page; Eligible FCT towers (PDF); Grants.gov listing
grants.Posting Date: September 24, 2026 (Grants.gov); FAA application period opened September 18, 2026

grants.Description: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency — 2026 Diesel Emissions Reduction Act (DERA) National Program
grants.Opportunity #: EPA-OAR-OTAQ-26-01; Assistance Listing 66.039 (Diesel Emission Reduction Act (DERA) National Grants). Grants.gov opportunity 363936.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency — Office of Air and Radiation. Questions to dera@epa.gov with the subject line "DERA National NOFO Question."
grants.Total Funding: Approximately $180,000,000, combining roughly $65M in FY 2024, $62M in FY 2025, and $53M in FY 2026 funds into a single competition. EPA anticipates 4–12 awards per EPA Region, with 2–4 year project periods.
grants.Award Range:
No stated minimum. Per-application caps are set by EPA Region, and requests over the cap are ineligible and will not be reviewed:

• Region 9 (California, Arizona, Hawaii, Nevada, Pacific Islands) — $42,600,000 regional allocation; $12,000,000 cap per application, the highest in the program.

• Region 2 (New York, New Jersey, Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands) — $18,300,000 regional allocation; $4,000,000 cap per application.

Other regional caps run from $3,000,000 (Region 1) to $8,000,000 (Region 5). An applicant may file up to two applications per region and ten in total, and each application must draw on a single region.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
• Regional, state, local, or tribal agencies and port authorities with jurisdiction over transportation or air quality. School districts, municipalities, MPOs, cities, and counties generally qualify.

• Nonprofits that provide pollution reduction or educational services to diesel fleet owners or operators, or whose principal purpose is promoting transportation or air quality. Institutions of higher education and government or nonprofit hospitals may qualify on the same terms.
grants.Deadline: January 22, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET. Written questions due November 24, 2026. Anticipated selection notification May 2027; anticipated award July 2027.
grants.Program Focus:
Retrofit or replacement of legacy diesel engines, vehicles, and equipment with EPA- or CARB-certified or verified technologies: school and transit buses, Class 5–8 trucks (including drayage), marine engines, locomotives, and nonroad equipment used in construction, cargo handling, agriculture, mining, and energy production.

EPA describes this NOFO as a revamp of prior rounds, and the scoring structure reflects it: priority goes to fleets operating at goods-movement facilities (ports, airports, rail yards, terminals, distribution centers) and in nonattainment or maintenance areas or counties with high modeled diesel PM. Zero-emission replacements remain eligible, but neither grant funds nor cost share may pay for charging or fueling infrastructure.

Existing units must be fully operational, owned and operated by the fleet for the prior two years, have at least three years of remaining life, and meet usage floors — for example, 7,000 miles per year for highway vehicles and 500 hours per year for most nonroad engines. Replaced engines must be scrapped within 90 days.
grants.Cost Share / Match:
Yes — mandatory and technology-specific, set out in NOFO Table 2. Examples:

• Highway vehicle replacement: EPA funds 25%, 35%, or 45% depending on the replacement engine's certified NOx level — the cleaner the engine, the higher the federal share.

• Nonroad, locomotive, or marine replacement with a certified engine: EPA 25% / recipient 75%.

• EPA- or CARB-verified exhaust after-treatment retrofits: 100% federal, no cost share.

Applicants that cannot identify a projected EPA engine family name at application are held to the lowest federal share for highway projects. Mandatory cost share must appear on the SF-424 and SF-424A, and federal environmental mitigation funds (such as the VW Mitigation Trust) cannot be counted toward it.
grants.Primary Sector: Clean Transportation; Diesel Emissions Reduction; Ports and Goods Movement; Fleet Replacement and Retrofit; Nonattainment Areas; Zero-Emission Vehicles
grants.Link to NOFO: DERA National on Simpler.Grants.gov; EPA-OAR-OTAQ-26-01 (PDF); EPA DERA National Program page; Grants.gov listing

grants.Description: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Geothermal — Geologic Enhanced Mapping System (GEMS) Prize
grants.Opportunity #: No NOFO number. Prize competition hosted on DrivenData (Competition 306); official rules posted on HeroX.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Energy — Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office, Office of Geothermal, with support from the National Lab of the Rockies (NLR). Questions to gemsprize@nlr.gov or the competition forum.
grants.Award Range:
$10,000 to $100,000, across two scoring rounds applied to the same submission:

• Initial Prize Round — top five on the private expert-labeled test set receive $10,000 each ($50,000 total).

• Final Prize Round — top five against an expanded label set built from expert review of all submissions: $100,000 / $70,000 / $40,000 / $25,000 / $15,000 ($250,000 total).

DOE's announcement describes prizes as ranging from $15,000 to $100,000; the DrivenData prize table shows $10,000 for each initial-round winner. The competition page is the operative source.
grants.Eligible Applicants: Individuals who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents; teams whose captain is a U.S. citizen or permanent resident; and private entities incorporated in and maintaining a primary place of business in the United States. Federal entities and federal employees are not eligible.
grants.Program Focus:
Develop, train, and test algorithms that generate enhanced geologic fault datasets from geophysical data — supporting discovery of hidden geothermal systems and critical-mineral mapping. Training data are the USGS Quaternary fault dataset; scoring is against newly identified faults in the GeoDAWN region, which overlaps spatially with the training set. Licensed external data are encouraged, and a reference solution is posted on GitHub.

This is a data-science competition, not a research grant. The best fit is a client with in-house machine learning and geospatial capability that can iterate against a leaderboard over the next ten weeks. DrivenData showed 288 participants enrolled as of this week.
grants.Funding Instrument: Prize — cash awards; no grant agreement, budget, or reporting.
grants.Primary Sector: Geothermal Exploration; Machine Learning and Geospatial Data Science; Fault Mapping; Critical Minerals; Federal Prize Competitions
grants.Link to Competition: DOE GEMS Prize announcement; GEMS Prize on DrivenData; Official rules (HeroX)

grants.Description: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Technology Commercialization — FY26 & FY27 Technology Commercialization Fund (TCF) CLIMR Lab Call: Technology Specific Topics
grants.Opportunity #: DE-LC-000L130. Companion to DE-LC-000L129, the FY26 CLIMR Commercialization Enabling Topic lab call issued February 18, 2026.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Energy — Office of Technology Commercialization (OTC), jointly with five DOE program offices, including the Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (CMEI) and the Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER). Questions to tcf@hq.doe.gov.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
DOE National Laboratories, plants, and sites only, with applications routed through each lab's Technology Transfer Office.

Companies, universities, and nonprofits cannot apply directly. They participate as lab partners and can register on the Teaming Partner List (TPL-0000077) so lab researchers can find them. Under the FY26 CLIMR framework, a technology counts as National Lab-developed only if at least 50% of its R&D was conducted at a National Laboratory, plant, or site.
grants.Deadline: Concept paper due 11/3/26 and full application due 3/1/27.
grants.Program Focus:
Advancing the commercialization of specific energy-related, National Lab-developed technologies by pairing technical progress with demonstrated market pull — in practice, lab–industry partnership projects. DOE split the FY26/FY27 CLIMR cycle into two calls; this is the second, technology-specific one.

For GMA clients this is a partnering play rather than an application. The move is to identify the lab inventor or technology the client wants to license, validate, or scale, and get the client on the Teaming Partner List now.
grants.Funding Instrument: Lab call — DOE funds flow to the laboratories, not to outside entities. Partner participation is typically documented through a CRADA or similar agreement with the lab.
grants.Cost Share / Match: Expect a non-federal partner contribution. The FY25 CLIMR selections leveraged more than $21 million in cost share from private and public partners against roughly $35 million in federal funds. Confirm the required percentage in the lab call.
grants.Primary Sector: Technology Transfer; National Laboratory Commercialization; Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation; Energy Security; Licensing and CRADAs
grants.Link to Solicitation: DOE Technology Commercialization Fund page; FY25 CLIMR project selections
grants.Posting Date: Released September 2026 per DOE's Notice of Intent; TCF program page updated September 24, 2026

grants.Description: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service — FY 2026 Easement Restoration and Stewardship
grants.Opportunity #: USDA-NHQ-ACEP-26-NOFO0001456; Assistance Listings 10.931 (Agricultural Conservation Easement Program), 10.928 (Emergency Watershed Protection Program – Floodplain Easements), and 10.072 (Wetlands Reserve Program). Grants.gov opportunity 363920.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Agriculture — Natural Resources Conservation Service; administered by the FPAC Business Center, Grants and Agreements Division. Contact Tessa Garcia, Grants Management Specialist, tessa.garcia@usda.gov, subject line “USDA-ACEP-NOFO0001456 Easement Stewardship and Restoration.” Applicants may not contact NRCS program staff directly.
grants.Total Funding: $5,000,000 expected, across one to four awards. NRCS retains discretion to award more or less.
grants.Award Range: $250,000 to $5,000,000. Projects should run four to five years, planned around an estimated March 1, 2027 start.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Broad: state, county, city, and special district governments; federally recognized tribes and other tribal organizations; nonprofits with or without 501(c)(3) status; public and private institutions of higher education; and for-profit firms, including small businesses.

Applications must come from a single entity — partners participate as subrecipients. Profit is not an allowable cost, so for-profit awardees are reimbursed for direct and indirect costs only. Indirect costs for nonprofits and universities are capped at 10% of total direct costs.
grants.Deadline:
November 19, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET via Grants.gov. No pre-application or letter of intent.

Selections anticipated January 2027; awards executed by March 2027.
grants.Program Focus:
Restoration, stewardship, and monitoring of lands under NRCS Wetland Reserve Easements (ACEP-WRE), legacy Wetlands Reserve Program easements, and Emergency Watershed Protection floodplain easements. Applicants may propose one, several, or all components:

• Engineering planning and design — topographic surveys, hydrologic and hydraulic modeling, stamped designs for practices such as dikes, water control structures, and wetland restoration, and construction bid packages;

• Vegetative restoration and stewardship — planting, re-establishment, and maintenance plans for easements with failed or degraded vegetation;

• Easement monitoring — onsite and offsite compliance and ecological-condition reviews, with remediation or enhancement plans where deficiencies are found.

Work is anticipated in all 50 states, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, and the Pacific Islands Area. Unless an applicant confines itself to a defined region, it must be available to coordinate projects nationwide. Specific easements are not identified until selection.

Scoring is capacity-driven: survey and design experience (20%), resource availability (20%), staff qualifications (20%), contractor oversight (15%), cost efficiency (10%), references (10%), and federal agreement administration (5%). That profile favors engineering and restoration firms with licensed staff and a track record of federal agreements.
grants.Funding Instrument: Cooperative agreement; NRCS may negotiate an alternate award type.
grants.Cost Share / Match: None required. Proposed cost share will not be considered in the competitive review.
grants.Primary Sector: Wetland Restoration; Floodplain Easements; Conservation Engineering; Easement Stewardship and Monitoring; Agricultural Conservation Easement Program
grants.Link to NOFO: Easement Restoration and Stewardship on Simpler.Grants.gov; USDA-NHQ-ACEP-26-NOFO0001456 (PDF); Grants.gov listing

grants.Description: California Energy Commission — GFO-26-502, Integrated Point-Source Carbon Capture and Advanced Combustion at Industrial Facilities
grants.Agency / Funder: California Natural Resources Agency. Contact (916) 653-2812, ycagrants@resources.ca.gov.
grants.Total Funding: Approximately $15,000,000 for local assistance, from Proposition 64 cannabis tax revenue (the Youth Education, Prevention, Early Intervention and Treatment Account).
grants.Eligible Applicants: Local and state public agencies, nonprofit organizations, and California Native American tribes. Statewide.
grants.Deadline:
November 4, 2026, 11:59 p.m. CNRA updated the deadline on September 21 — confirm against the current guidelines.

Expected award announcement April 2027; projects must be completed by March 1, 2030.
grants.Program Focus:
Projects that give youth from low-income and disadvantaged communities immersive, meaningful experiences with natural or cultural resources in California that they otherwise would not have.

The guidelines define “low-income and disadvantaged” by disproportionate lack of access to natural and cultural resources — read that definition before scoping the target population.

Because the funding comes from Prop 64’s youth substance-use prevention account, framing access to nature and culture as a protective, prevention-oriented activity may strengthen alignment with the program’s statutory purpose.
grants.Funding Instrument: Grant; reimbursement, with 10% retained until completion. Advances of up to 25% are allowed in certain circumstances.
grants.Primary Sector: Youth Outdoor Access; Environmental and Cultural Education; Parks and Recreation; Disadvantaged Communities; Proposition 64
grants.Link to Solicitation: YCA Round 4 on the California Grants Portal; CNRA YCA grant guidelines; RAPTR application portal

grants.Description: NYSERDA — Buildings of Excellence Competition, Round 7
grants.Agency / Funder: NYSERDA, in partnership with the New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets. Contacts: Kristin France and Gabrielle Lafyatis (emails on the solicitation page).
grants.Total Funding: $10,000,000 multi-year program, per NYSERDA’s launch announcement. Round-by-round allocation is in the PON Summary.
grants.Award Range: Depends on project. Multiple awards anticipated per proposal type.
grants.Eligible Applicants: Farmers, solar developers, communities, supporting organizations, and businesses. Projects must be in New York State; a Site Control and Access Form (Attachment C) is part of the application.
grants.Program Focus:
Integration of solar energy with active agriculture — agrivoltaics — so farmers gain income and lower energy costs while keeping land in production. The program was launched in the 2026 State of the State. Eligible proposals:

• Planning, feasibility, and initial-preparation projects — agrivoltaics for on-farm power or grid export, and solar-plus-storage for on-farm energy use;

• Implementation and scaling projects — new or adapted technologies, equipment, or agricultural practices; novel configurations or retrofits of existing solar; or farm types and regions where agrivoltaics is not yet common;

• Applied research, market solutions, guidance, training, and capacity building that address barriers to integrating solar and agriculture.

Up to $10,000,000 is available through this PON for projects in four categories: (A) Solar and Agriculture Integration – On-the-Ground Projects; (B) Addressing Barriers and Challenges, Creating Opportunities for Solar and Agriculture Integration; (C) Building Capacity and Support for Farmers and Communities; and (D) Increasing Opportunities and Access within the Integration of Solar Energy Infrastructure and Agriculture.
grants.Funding Instrument: NYSERDA agreement (sample agreement posted as Attachment B).
grants.Primary Sector: Agrivoltaics; On-Farm Solar and Battery Storage; Farmland Preservation; Agricultural Energy Costs; Applied Research
grants.Link to Solicitation: PON 6206 solicitation page; PON 6206 Summary (PDF); Sun and Soil program page
grants.Posting Date: Not stated on the solicitation page
